title: LearnGraph: A Learning-Based Architecture for Dynamic Graph Processing
problem: Dynamic graph processing systems using conventional array-based architectures suffer from inefficient memory access patterns and poor index management, limiting throughput.
motivation: Learned indexes improve data structure access, but interconnected graph data requires specialized adaptive structures to exploit topology and access patterns.
method: Proposes an adaptive tree-based memory manager with two components: (1) hierarchical learned index optimized for graph topology to predict vertex and edge locations, and (2) adaptive tree structure that dynamically reorganizes memory regions based on access patterns.
key_novelty: Integration of learned indexes with topology-aware adaptive memory reorganization for dynamic graph systems.
contributions: Hierarchical learned index architecture tailored for graph vertex/edge prediction
Adaptive tree-based memory manager that reorganizes regions based on runtime access patterns
3.4x higher throughput on average and 1.7x-11x reduction in processing time over state-of-the-art systems

metrics.speedup: 3.4x higher throughput; 1.7x-11x reduction in processing time

limitations: Not discussed—no analysis of memory overhead or scalability limits.
primary_theme: Learned-index–driven adaptive memory architecture for graphs
